sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Establishment**: Founded in **1988** by the **World Meteorological Organization (WMO)** and the **United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)**.
• **Mandate**: Does not conduct original research; it **synthesizes and evaluates** existing peer-reviewed scientific, technical, and socio-economic literature.
• **Membership**: Open to all member countries of the **UN and WMO** (195 members).
• **Key Metric**: Produces **Assessment Reports (AR)**, Special Reports, and Methodology Reports which serve as the 'Gold Standard' for global climate policy.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Atmospheric physics, oceanography, and paleoclimate data
Basis for understanding 'Tipping Points' and 'Carbon Budgets'
Crucial for Mains answers on Disaster Management and Agriculture
Directly linked to NDCs and Net-Zero targets

items.definition: Comprehensive reviews published every 5-7 years. AR6 (2021-2023) is the current reference point for global climate action.
A high-level document approved line-by-line by member governments, ensuring political consensus on scientific findings.
Targeted reports on specific issues (e.g., Global Warming of 1.5°C, Ocean and Cryosphere, Land Use).

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Carbon Budgeting**: Defining the remaining CO2 emissions allowed to stay within 1.5°C or 2°C warming.
• **Policy Guidance**: Provides the scientific basis for the 'Global Stocktake' under the Paris Agreement.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Political pressure during SPM approval; lag between scientific discovery and policy implementation.
• **Solutions**: Increased focus on regional climate modeling and integration of indigenous knowledge systems.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'P-I-A-M' (Physical, Impacts, Adaptation, Mitigation).
• **Decoded Meaning**: WGI (Physical Science), WGII (Impacts & Adaptation), WGIII (Mitigation).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: The IPCC does NOT prescribe specific policies to countries; it provides 'policy-relevant' but 'policy-neutral' information. It does not mandate laws.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Science-Policy Interface' when discussing the IPCC's role in global governance.

keyTakeaways: IPCC is a scientific body, not a political one; it provides the evidence base for UNFCCC negotiations.
It is co-sponsored by WMO and UNEP, not a standalone UN agency.
The 'Summary for Policymakers' is the only part of the report that requires intergovernmental approval.
